definition: NVIDIA's GPU library of basic linear-algebra routines, above all matrix multiplication (GEMM). Most AI frameworks send their big matrix multiplies to it.

NVIDIA's open-source collection of CUDA C++ templates for building custom high-performance matrix-multiply and related kernels, used when the stock cuBLAS routine does not fit (new number formats, fused operations).
The layout-and-tensor abstraction at the core of CUTLASS 3 and 4. It describes how data is tiled across threads and memory, and since CUTLASS 4 it is also available as a Python DSL.
A small programming language designed for one job. CuTe DSL, Triton and Mojo are DSLs for writing GPU kernels without full C++.
NVIDIA's library for linear algebra on sparse matrices (mostly zeros), used in simulation, graph analytics and recommendation models.
NVIDIA's fast Fourier transform library, used in signal processing, imaging, seismic analysis and physics codes.
NVIDIA's random-number-generation library, used for Monte Carlo simulation, risk models and the random initialisation of neural networks.

NVIDIA's inference optimizer and runtime: it takes a trained model, fuses and quantizes its operations and produces an engine tuned for a specific NVIDIA GPU. TensorRT-LLM is its large-language-model branch.
NVIDIA's open-source suite of GPU data-science libraries launched in 2018 (cuDF, cuML, cuGraph, cuVS and others) that mirror popular Python tools such as pandas and scikit-learn.
The RAPIDS GPU dataframe library: a pandas-like table engine that also powers GPU back ends for Spark, Polars and Dask.
A cuDF mode that accelerates unchanged pandas code: operations the GPU supports run there, everything else falls back to normal pandas on the CPU.
The RAPIDS GPU machine-learning library (random forests, clustering, UMAP and similar). Its cuml.accel mode runs unchanged scikit-learn code on the GPU.
The RAPIDS GPU graph-analytics library (PageRank, shortest paths, community detection) for networks with billions of edges.
NVIDIA's GPU library for vector search (finding the nearest embeddings) and clustering, built into Faiss, Milvus and other vector databases.
NVIDIA's GPU optimization engine for linear programming and vehicle routing, open-sourced under Apache 2.0 in 2025.
NVIDIA's libraries for simulating quantum computers on GPUs (state-vector and tensor-network methods), used to develop and test quantum algorithms.
NVIDIA's open platform and compiler for hybrid quantum-classical programs that run across quantum processors, GPUs and CPUs.
NVIDIA's library for computational lithography: the heavy calculations that shape photomask patterns so chips print correctly. TSMC put it into production with Synopsys in 2024.
Software that pre-distorts chip-design patterns on a photomask (optical proximity correction) so they print accurately on the wafer; one of the largest compute workloads in chip manufacturing.

An open-source Python framework from NVIDIA that compiles ordinary Python functions into GPU kernels for physics simulation, robotics and differentiable programming. Not to be confused with a GPU warp of 32 threads.
The physics engine NVIDIA gained with Ageia in 2008, used in games, robotics simulation and Omniverse; now open source.
NVIDIA's platform for building 3D simulations and digital twins of factories, robots and data centers, built on OpenUSD and PhysX.
NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated genomics software, which runs standard DNA-sequencing pipelines (alignment, variant calling) many times faster than CPU tools.
The step in genome analysis that finds where a person's DNA differs from the reference genome; the compute-heavy core of clinical sequencing pipelines.
NVIDIA's framework and model collection for training and serving biology and chemistry foundation models (proteins, molecules, DNA).
NVIDIA's platform for AI weather and climate models and digital twins of the Earth; Earth2Studio is its open-source Python package.
Finding the stored items whose embeddings (lists of numbers that encode meaning) are closest to a query; the retrieval step in RAG and recommendation systems.
Finding the best value of a linear objective (cost, profit) subject to linear constraints; the workhorse of logistics, scheduling and supply-chain planning.
A table of rows and named columns held in memory, the basic data structure of pandas, Polars and Spark.
The data-preparation work of pulling raw data from sources, cleaning and joining it, and loading it into a warehouse or training set; often the largest analytics bill in an enterprise.
The most widely used open-source engine for large-scale data processing and SQL across clusters of servers.
A standard decision-support benchmark of about 100 SQL queries over retail-style data. Vendor tests 'derived from' it are not official, audited TPC results.
Running existing code (pandas, scikit-learn, Polars, Spark) on GPUs by swapping the engine underneath, with no rewrite and automatic CPU fallback for unsupported operations.
In-network reduction inside NVLink switches: the switch adds up data from all GPUs and multicasts the result, so an all-reduce sends each GPU's data about once instead of about twice.
An all-reduce that sums data up a tree of nodes and broadcasts it back down. It needs about 2·log2(N) hops instead of a ring's 2(N−1), so it has far lower latency at scale.
An NCCL algorithm (2024) for all-gather and reduce-scatter at very large scale that uses a logarithmic number of steps, cutting latency when each GPU sends little data.
The metric NCCL's benchmark reports: the data rate each GPU's links actually sustain during a collective, normalised so it can be compared with the hardware link speed.
Letting a GPU kernel post network transfers itself instead of waiting for the CPU to do it; NCCL 2.28 added this (GIN) to cut latency for MoE and inference traffic.
AMD's ROCm Communication Collectives Library, derived from NCCL's code and API, which runs collectives on Instinct GPUs over Infinity Fabric and networks.
Microsoft's open-source GPU communication stack that lets developers write custom collective algorithms with one-sided GPU-driven primitives; it runs on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.
Meta's open-source collective-communication library, a PyTorch back end mainly used for CPU tensors and as a fallback when NCCL is unavailable.
The decades-old standard for communication between processes in supercomputing; NCCL can run inside MPI applications, and MPI libraries can call NCCL for GPU data.
An open-source collective library from the Unified Communication Framework consortium that targets HPC and AI and treats hardware-offloaded collectives as first-class.
